done_when: A repo lists tests every change must run in forge.toml's always_test, close runs them locally beside the picked tests, and this repo lists its rules, every-refusal and view-contract tests

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Functional
The generated selection hook checks that each entry was collected, but it does not check that the entry remains selected after other collection hooks run. For a repo whose test command uses `-k` or `-m`, pytest can deselect a listed test afterward; another picked test can pass and close can report success without running the listed test. Pytest applies those filters in its [mark hook](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pytest-dev/pytest/main/src/_pytest/mark/__init__.py), and [hook ordering](https://pluggy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/) permits the later registered Forge hook to run first. The refusal proof does not cover a collected entry that is subsequently deselected.
findings.title: Close can succeed after pytest filters out an always_test entry

stop.reason: Coordinator (Harm 2, reversible; third finding in fasttest.py, so replace the cases with one general rule): close passes every always_test entry to pytest explicitly as its own argument, whatever the test command's roots, and fails when any entry collects no test. No more per-layout cases.

why: Close picks local tests by imports and mentions, so cross-cutting tests such as the rules and every-refusal checks fail only in CI, a round later
